text:
sanjay: Quick heads-up — ran a perf sweep on fp8/int8/4bit kernels with the new dataset-slicing heuristics. Found a weird tail regression on the int8 decode path.
anya: Can you paste the raw perf numbers and the slice config?
sanjay: nvprof-ish samples (mini-run): fp32_gemm ~2.4ms, fp8_gemm ~1.1ms, int8_gemm ~1.3ms, int4_gemm ~0.9ms. But observed P99 decode for int8 is +18% vs fp8 when KV cache is hot.
mike: Hot KV makes the decoder sensitive to memory access patterns — did the kernel chooser fall back to a different kernel variant?
sanjay: Yes — for certain sequence buckets it picks a different fused-kv path. Hypothesis: our per-tensor calibration produced wider scales on some attention heads -> larger activations -> kernel selects slower path under the allocator's heuristics.
ellen: Which calibration dataset did you use? full-sample or stratified? Any outlier handling?
sanjay: Single-pass sampled 5k prompts uniform over top-level categories, but NOT stratified by seq-length or prefix token distribution. No extreme outlier clipping. Tail ended up with many long-form code prompts.
anya: That explains it. Outlier-heavy slices change the quantization range a lot. Can we try per-channel calibration for attention matrices and per-tensor for MLP? Quick A/B.
mike: Also try reweighting slices: upweight seq>512 and rare-token buckets. Outliers should be downweighted or clipped (e.g., 99.9p).
sanjay: Ran a quick job with slice-weighting + per-channel on attn. Command used:
```bash
tools/calib/run.sh --slices 'seq:>512:weight=3,rare:top0.1p:weight=4' --mode per-channel --clip 99.9
```
sanjay: Result: int8 P99 decode regression reduced from +18% to +4% relative to fp8, but int4 shows a correctness dip for long-form code.
ellen: How big is the correctness drop for int4?
sanjay: Eval (codegen set): fp8 baseline delta 0.0, int8 +0.2 (tiny), int4 -1.2 relative BLEU-ish metric on long-code prompts.
anya: So a mixed-precision plan might make sense: keep fp8 for attention, int4 for MLP, with per-channel calib for attention only. That preserves latency wins while limiting quality loss.
mike: Agrees. Attention weights are more sensitive to per-channel scaling. Also we should ensure kernel-selection has a forced override for long sequences until we validate (i.e., prefer fp8_gemm when seq>1024).
perf-bot: perf-alert: regression detected in /eng-ml/trafficsweep — created ticket CD-482 with linked traces.
sanjay: I created CD-482, attached trace snippets and the calib config used.
ellen: For rollout: propose canary at 5% with automatic fallback to fp8 on tail alarm (P99 threshold) and an accuracy smoke check on the eval set.
anya: +1. Also add a kernel-selection pin: runtime rule to prefer fp8_gemm for kv_cache_hot && seq>1024.
mike: I'll prototype that routing rule in runtime and extend trace logs to include per-kernel latencies and chosen variant ids.
sanjay: Next steps for me: run a 20k-sample stratified sweep (seq, prefix token distribution, domain) with outlier clipping (percentile 99.9) and warm-start per-channel scales for attention. Post results to CD-482.
ellen: SGTM — I'll own the canary runbook and alarm thresholds.
mike: I'll add perf harness changes to capture microsecond breakdown per kernel and add a quick dashboard tile.
anya: Thanks all — good progress. :thumbsup:
